tweet.text:
llama.cpp has three main points that makes me a huge fan of it:

Runs almost anywhere with almost nothing because it is pure C/C++, no heavy dependencies (no PyTorch, no CUDA required). Runs on CPU-only, Apple Silicon, old GPUs, even phones and Raspberry Pis.

Quantization using GGUF format with formats like Q4_K_M, Q8_0, etc. lets you shrink models 4-8x with surprisingly small quality loss. This is the reason you can run a 35B MoE model on your 3090/3060 setup at all.

Fine-grained control over hardware split with flags like -ngl, --n-cpu-moe, -ctk/-ctv let you decide exactly what lives on GPU vs CPU, tune KV cache precision separately, and squeeze out every bit of VRAM. For MoE models especially, offloading just the active experts to GPU while parking the rest on CPU RAM is a huge win, it’s basically why hobbyist local MoE inference is viable at all right now.
